first_impression.reaction: I searched 'getting married in brazil' because Trancoso keeps turning up on my Pinterest board. The intro answers the legal question straight away. No 'fairytale', no 'paradise', so I kept going. The legal order is genuinely useful. But nearly every section ends with 'ask the cartório' or 'ask your venue', and the residence rule is a real worry: if neither of us lives in Brazil, can we even apply? By the end I knew what to ask. I still didn't know if Brazil works for 80 guests and my grandparents, or roughly what it costs.

journey.quote: What follows is the order to work in: documents first, then the cartório, then the certificate you bring home.
journey.reaction: Calm and organised. This is the spreadsheet I don't want to build myself. Good start.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Brazil?
journey.quote: If neither of you lives in Brazil, ask the registry office directly how it applies the district rule to couples who live abroad, and which office should take your application.
journey.reaction: Hang on. That's the one thing I needed answered, and it's handed back to us. Neither of us lives in Brazil. Is this a real hurdle or a formality? I'd want someone who has actually done it to tell me.

journey.quote: In Brazil, foreign documents, even when apostilled, must be translated by a tradutor juramentado, a sworn public translator, to be valid, and that translation can only be done in Brazil.
journey.reaction: I'd never have known that. It changes how early we fly in. This is the insider detail I'm looking for.

journey.quote: Embassy staff will not say which documents you need, and a CNI application mailed from within Brazil is accepted only if a local notary at a cartório witnessed the signature.
journey.reaction: Honest and specific, but a bit alarming. If even the embassy won't tell us, who will? This is exactly where I'd want a planner to say 'we handle this'.

journey.section: A religious ceremony with civil effect
journey.quote: Agree with your celebrant, in writing, who will lodge it and when.
journey.reaction: Practical and the sort of thing that goes wrong with no one accountable. Going in the planning doc.

journey.quote: So a ceremony on sand, a clifftop lawn or a fazenda veranda starts as a conversation with the cartório.
journey.reaction: Then two lists of questions. Useful, but by now it's the fifth list of questions. I wanted a sense of whether beach ceremonies are normal there or a battle.

journey.quote: For Australians: you need a visa to enter Brazil and must arrange it before arrival; it cannot be obtained at the airport, and travellers who arrive without one are sent back on the next available flight.
journey.reaction: Very good to know. My uncle would absolutely turn up without one. This goes straight in the guest info pack.

journey.quote: It says violent crime including mugging, armed robbery and carjacking is common, more often in large cities and during festivals such as Carnival, and advises against going out alone at night and against isolated areas, including beaches.
journey.reaction: Honest, and I'd rather know. But Mum reads this and Brazil is off the list. There's nothing telling me how couples actually keep 80 guests safe in practice.

journey.quote: **Security:** how does your security work for any couple marrying here, and how would it work alongside security we bring?
journey.reaction: Security we bring? We're not bringing bodyguards. Reads like it's written for someone else.

journey.section: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
journey.quote: The cost turns on where you marry, how many guests travel, how many nights you take a property and whether the legal ceremony comes to your venue.
journey.reaction: The heading promised a cost and there isn't a single number. Not even a range. This is the section Dad would read first.

journey.quote: Smartraveller names Copacabana Beach, Ipanema Beach, the Pedra do Sal area, Santa Teresa, Lapa, the Christ the Redeemer statue and the Corcovado Trail as crime hotspots.
journey.reaction: So the Rio section is mostly rain, rips and crime. Fair, but it reads like a warning, not a reason to go. I've no idea why anyone would choose Rio over Trancoso.

journey.quote: Ask your venue how guests reach it from the nearest airport, and how long the transfer takes after dark.
journey.reaction: This is our biggest worry, grandparents from the airport to the venue, and once again it's handed back to us. No airport named, no drive time.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and fee in writing are the right reassurances. But after a whole page of 'ask the cartório', I want to know: will you do the cartório bit for us? Who is actually on the ground in Brazil?

journey.section: Plan your Brazil wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Everything around it is where the planning begins.
journey.reaction: Calm close, no hard sell. The one-line summary of the legal order is handy to send James.

turn_offs_found.quote: The cost turns on where you marry, how many guests travel, how many nights you take a property and whether the legal ceremony comes to your venue.
turn_offs_found.why: Vague pricing with no range under a heading that promises cost. Feeds our hidden-costs and currency fear and makes me suspect the number is scary.

turn_offs_found.quote: **Security:** how does your security work for any couple marrying here, and how would it work alongside security we bring?
turn_offs_found.why: Assumes we travel with our own security. Pitched at a celebrity-type client, so the list doesn't feel written for us and would look showy forwarded to friends.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Start to finish' is the generic end-to-end claim. After a page telling us to ask the cartório ourselves, it doesn't say what the Advisor actually takes off our plate in Brazil or who is accountable on the day.

would_share_with: James: the 'What documents do you need to marry in Brazil?' section and the closing summary, because the in-Brazil sworn translation and visa rule decide how early we fly in
My parents: the intro and 'Will a Brazilian marriage be recognised in Australia?', because Dad will ask if it's legal at home. I would not send the Safety or Rio sections to Mum yet

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan it with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-brazil&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: No pressure, and AUD plus fee in writing are right. But Brazil now feels like more paperwork and more risk than I'd assumed, with no price range, no airport or transfer detail and no real Brazil wedding to look at. I'd want to see you've done one there before enquiring.

top_3_changes: Answer the residence worry, or at least frame it: 'If neither of you lives in Brazil, ask the registry office directly how it applies the district rule to couples who live abroad, and which office should take your application.' leaves us unsure we can marry legally at all. Say plainly whether this is a common hurdle, and that a Wedded Advisor can take it up with the cartório for us if that's true.

Give the cost section something to hold: 'The cost turns on where you marry...' under a cost heading reads evasive. Add at least a From AUD range (with sign-off) or say clearly that venue pricing is not published and how we get it.

Make the regions and safety sections help us choose, not just warn: name arrival airports and rough transfers for Trancoso, Paraty and Búzios, and drop 'alongside security we bring', which doesn't fit couples like us.

open_questions.question: Does the source pack confirm how cartórios treat non-resident couples under the district rule? It is the biggest open worry for this couple.
Is a From AUD range available for sign-off, or should the cost section say pricing is not published and how to get it?
The 'security we bring' line misses this persona again, as on New Zealand and Costa Rica. Is it meant for a different persona?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'getting married in brazil' with Brazil as an early idea rather than a shortlist, so relevance is 3 and enquiry likelihood is 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).
Business details and fee amounts are deliberately deferred and not penalised as must-fix.
Fast-mode read covered the intro, legal, documents, ceremony, recognition, entry, safety, cost, regions, venues and close; the FAQ was skimmed.
